title: Brent Tops $89 Amid U.S.-Iran Stalemate Over Hormuz
author: Tsvetana Paraskova
excerpt: Brent Crude oil prices rose above $89 per barrel in early trade in Europe on Wednesday as Iran and the United States offered contrasting claims about who controls the Strait of Hormuz. Brent Crude prices were up by 0.64% at $89.60 in the morning in Europe, and WTI Crude was rising by 0.94% at $83.90
content:
By Tsvetana Paraskova - Aug 12, 2026, 4:30 AM CDT

  • Brent crude climbed above $89 per barrel as traders continued to price in disruption risks around the Strait of Hormuz.
  • Iran says Hormuz will remain closed unless Washington meets its conditions, while President Trump says the United States has “total control” of the waterway.
  • US officials say regional oil flows have normalized, but depressed vessel traffic and continuing security risks leave that claim open to challenge.

Brent Crude oil prices rose above $89 per barrel in early trade in Europe on Wednesday as Iran and the United States offered contrasting claims about who controls the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent Crude prices were up by 0.64% at $89.60 in the morning in Europe, and WTI Crude was rising by 0.94% at $83.90, amid persistent supply concerns and risks despite claims from the U.S. that traffic at Hormuz had normalized.

Iran, for its part, said on Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed unless the United States ends the war and meets Tehran’s conditions, raising the bar for a deal that would restore more oil traffic through the key waterway.

Later on Tuesday, U.S. President Donald Trump said that the United States had “total control over the Hormuz Strait,” in a claim that contrasts with Iran’s assertion that Tehran decides when and under what conditions the Strait would be closed or open.  

“We own it,” President Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.  

“And at some point, maybe they’ll do something, and then they get blown away,” the President said, referring to Iran.

Despite claims of talks in recent days, the U.S. and Iran appear to be at a stalemate, according to Wendy Sherman, former U.S. deputy secretary of state.

“Unless the US is ready to either allow Iran and perhaps Oman to have voluntary tolls or to give Iran so much relief from sanctions and frozen assets that it’s worth their while, I don’t think we’ll get it open for any sustainable period of time,” Sherman told Bloomberg TV.

Oil flows from the Middle East have normalized, with Sunday traffic alone above pre-conflict averages, U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said on Tuesday in a claim that appears not to be backed by ship-tracking data.

Traffic at the Strait of Hormuz has declined this week amid heightened security concerns and uncertainties about any U.S.-Iran talks.

By Tsvetana Paraskova for Oilprice.com

title: Tanker Data Contradicts U.S. Claim That Middle East Oil Flows Have Normalized
author: Tsvetana Paraskova
excerpt: Oil flows from the Middle East have normalized, with Sunday traffic alone above pre-conflict averages, U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said on Tuesday in a claim that appears not to be backed by ship-tracking data. On Tuesday, Secretary Wright posted on X that “Thanks to the coordinated effort
content:
Oil flows from the Middle East have normalized, with Sunday traffic alone above pre-conflict averages, U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said on Tuesday in a claim that appears not to be backed by ship-tracking data.

On Tuesday, Secretary Wright posted on X that “Thanks to the coordinated efforts of the U.S. military and our gulf allies, the seven-day average for oil leaving the Strait of Hormuz is currently up to almost 9 million barrels per day.”

He went on to add that “When combined with the additional 5-7 million barrels per day leaving the region via newly upgraded pipelines and export facilities, total oil flows are currently averaging approximately 15 million barrels per day.”  

According to the top U.S. energy official, “On Sunday alone, over 20 million barrels left the Arabian gulf region, which is above the pre-conflict average.”

However, analysts and tanker traffic monitoring services cannot fathom how the U.S. Administration has arrived at these numbers, considering that traffic at the Strait of Hormuz is severely constrained, even according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA).

“We have increased our estimates of Middle East shut-in crude oil production in the coming months compared with our July forecast due to continued severe constraints on Strait of Hormuz transits, which we assume persist through August,” the EIA said on Tuesday in its latest monthly Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO).

“It is not possible to reconcile the disparity between what we see and what he is quoting,” Matt Smith, director of commodity research at Kpler, told CNN, commenting on Wright’s claim.

Kpler data showed earlier this week that vessel traffic at the Strait of Hormuz continues to decline as last week’s hopes of negotiations of a U.S.-Iran deal began to fade, yet again.  

On Monday, only six commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz in either direction, down from 11 ships in the latest 10-day average, according to shipping data from Kpler cited by Reuters on Tuesday.

By Tsvetana Paraskova for Oilprice.com

title: North Dakota Department Of Agriculture Opens Hay Hotline
author: Jesse Allen
excerpt: Photo by Kayleigh Omang, 2023(Bismarck, ND) — The Hay Hotline is back in North Dakota. It’s an opportunity for ranchers to request hay or list a surplus of hay for sale or donation. The North Dakota Department
content:
Photo by Kayleigh Omang, 2023

(Bismarck, ND) — The Hay Hotline is back in North Dakota. It’s an opportunity for ranchers to request hay or list a surplus of hay for sale or donation. The North Dakota Department of Agriculture provides a list of locations where ranchers can find hay resources on its website. The department is also asking producers to report drought conditions to the National Drought Mitigation Center.

“Ranchers who need hay, or those with hay to sell or with pasture or hayland to rent may use our online form and map, or give us a call,” says Ag Commissioner Doug Goehring. “Your name and information will be entered into the Hay Hotline database to be matched up with others.”

To view hay, pasture and hayland available, producers may visit the self-service Hay Hotline map. To list any of those resources, producers may utilize the Hay Hotline online form. A special Hay Hotline program number is also available at 701-328-5110, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

SOURCE: ND Department of Agriculture

title: Farmers Harvest Wheat Early This Year in North Dakota
author: Jesse Allen
excerpt: (Wilton, ND) — Our scorching summer is forcing some North Dakota farmers to harvest earlier than usual. The USDA’s latest report shows about 20 percent of the state’s spring wheat crop has been harvested; that’s well ahead
content:
(Wilton, ND) — Our scorching summer is forcing some North Dakota farmers to harvest earlier than usual. The USDA’s latest report shows about 20 percent of the state’s spring wheat crop has been harvested; that’s well ahead of the average. Producers credit the hot, dry weather for pushing crops to mature earlier and for producing bumper crops. Spring wheat yields have been surprisingly good, averaging as much as 50 bushels per acre. But soybeans and corn may not fare as well unless we get some rain soon. One producer said, while he doesn’t have any corn planted, he’s noticed similar signs of stress in nearby cornfields too.
